Leave-one-subject-out jackknife of a NONMEM model

Source: R/nm_jackknife.R
nm_jackknife.Rd

Removes one subject at a time from the data set, re-estimates the model with NONMEM and measures how much each subject influences the fit. The primary metric is the likelihood influence \(|\Delta OFV| = |OFV_{(-i)} - OFV_{ref}|\); the secondary metrics are the relative THETA shifts \((\theta_{(-i)} - \theta_{ref}) / \theta_{ref}\), their L2 norm, their maximum, and an L2 norm standardised by the reference standard errors when the reference covariance step is usable. Subjects are ranked by \(|\Delta OFV|\). The analysis is descriptive (an influence diagnostic, not a formal outlier test).

Usage

nm_jackknife(
  ctl,
  nmfe_path = NULL,
  lst = NULL,
  reference_data = NULL,
  id_col = "ID",
  comment_char = NULL,
  sep = ",",
  output_dir = NULL,
  overwrite_existing_runs = FALSE,
  strip_tables = TRUE,
  strip_cov = FALSE,
  dtheta_threshold = 0.01,
  save_figures = TRUE,
  run = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  n_cores = 1L
)

# S3 method for class 'nm_jackknife'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

ctl

Path to the reference control stream (.ctl), already run.

nmfe_path

Path to the nmfe launcher (e.g. "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat" on Windows, "/opt/nm760/run/nmfe76" on Linux or macOS). Needed when run = TRUE.

lst

Reference output. Default: the .lst of the same name next to ctl.

reference_data

Data file. NULL (default): read from $DATA.

id_col

Label of the subject column in $INPUT (default "ID").

comment_char

Data comment/ignore character. NULL (default): the single-character IGNORE of $DATA ("#", "@", a letter...); "": none.

sep

Field separator of the data file (default ",").

output_dir

Working directory (default "<ctl_dir>/<run>_jackknife"). Holds jk_data/, jk_ctl/, jk_run/ (one subdirectory per run), figures/ and the two CSV files.

overwrite_existing_runs

FALSE (default): skip the runs already minimised (resume).

strip_tables

Remove $TABLE from the jackknife control streams (default TRUE).

strip_cov

Remove $COVARIANCE from the jackknife runs (default FALSE). TRUE is faster and does not change the influence metrics (the reference SE come from the reference run).

dtheta_threshold

Relative THETA shift flagged as large (default 0.01).

save_figures

Write the three figures to output_dir/figures (default TRUE).

run

FALSE: only write the data sets and control streams (no NONMEM).

verbose

Progress messages (default TRUE).

n_cores

Number of jackknife runs at the same time (default 1). A whole number, "auto" (physical cores minus one, see nm_cores()) or "ask" (interactive sessions: the cores are shown and the number is asked once per R session, then reused; options(nmpilot.n_cores = NULL) asks again). Each run is then started in the background in its own directory; if R is interrupted, the runs already started go on in the background and a later call with the same arguments picks up their results.

x

An nm_jackknife object.

digits

Significant digits in the printed table (default 4).

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class nm_jackknife: the reference OFV, THETA and SE, all_runs (every replicate, including the failed ones), summary (successful runs ranked by \(|\Delta OFV|\), with rank, rank_dtheta and, when available, rank_dtheta_z) and the settings. jackknife_all_runs.csv and jackknife_summary.csv are written to output_dir.

Details

The method is that of the standalone script nonmem-jackknife-influence (Simon N, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22257994). The data lines are copied verbatim (positional reading through $INPUT), so number formatting and rows removed by a conditional IGNORE=(...) are preserved. Runs already minimised are skipped on a second call (resume), unless overwrite_existing_runs = TRUE.

See also

nm_bootstrap(), nm_profile()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
jk <- nm_jackknife("C:/study/run2.reg/run2.ctl",
                   nmfe_path = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat")
jk
plot(jk, "bar")
plot(jk, "scatter")
} # }
